mcqs.question: When adding two vectors \(\vec A\) and \(\vec B\) graphically using the tip‑to‑tail method, which statement is correct?

options.A: The magnitude of the resultant is always the sum of the magnitudes of \(\vec A\) and \(\vec B\).
options.B: The resultant vector is drawn from the tail of \(\vec A\) to the tip of \(\vec B\).
options.C: The direction of the resultant is always the same as the direction of \(\vec A\).
options.D: The resultant is independent of the angle between \(\vec A\) and \(\vec B\).

mcqs.answer: The resultant vector is drawn from the tail of \(\vec A\) to the tip of \(\vec B\).
mcqs.explanation: In the tip‑to‑tail (head‑to‑tail) graphical method, \(\vec A\) is placed first, then \(\vec B\) is placed so that its tail starts at the tip of \(\vec A\). The resultant is the vector drawn from the free tail of \(\vec A\) to the free tip of \(\vec B\). The magnitude depends on the angle between the vectors, so options A, C and D are misconceptions.

mcqs.question: Vector \(\vec C = \vec A - \vec B\). Which construction correctly represents \(\vec C\) using the graphical method?

options.A: Place the tail of \(\vec B\) at the tip of \(\vec A\); draw \(\vec C\) from the tail of \(\vec A\) to the tip of \(\vec B\).
options.B: Place the tip of \(\vec B\) at the tip of \(\vec A\); draw \(\vec C\) from the tail of \(\vec A\) to the tip of \(\vec B\).
options.C: Place the tail of \(\vec B\) at the tail of \(\vec A\); draw \(\vec C\) from the tip of \(\vec A\) to the tip of \(\vec B\).
options.D: Place the tip of \(\vec B\) at the tail of \(\vec A\); draw \(\vec C\) from the tail of \(\vec B\) to the tip of \(\vec A\).

mcqs.answer: Place the tip of \(\vec B\) at the tail of \(\vec A\); draw \(\vec C\) from the tail of \(\vec B\) to the tip of \(\vec A\).
mcqs.explanation: Subtracting \(\vec B\) from \(\vec A\) is equivalent to adding \(\vec A\) and \(-\vec B\). The vector \(-\vec B\) has the same magnitude as \(\vec B\) but opposite direction, so its tail is placed at the tip of \(\vec A\). Graphically, this is achieved by placing the tip of \(\vec B\) at the tail of \(\vec A\) and then drawing the resultant from the tail of \(\vec B\) (which is now the starting point) to the tip of \(\vec A\). Options A, B, and C do not follow the correct construction for subtraction.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the triangle law of vector addition from the component method?

options.A: The triangle law requires vectors to be placed head‑to‑tail, while the component method adds magnitudes algebraically without regard to direction.
options.B: Both methods give the same resultant, but the triangle law cannot be used when the vectors are not coplanar.
options.C: In the triangle law the resultant is obtained by completing a triangle, whereas in the component method each vector is resolved into perpendicular components before algebraic addition.
options.D: The triangle law is applicable only for forces, whereas the component method can be used for any type of vector.

mcqs.answer: In the triangle law the resultant is obtained by completing a triangle, whereas in the component method each vector is resolved into perpendicular components before algebraic addition.
mcqs.explanation: The triangle (or head‑to‑tail) law constructs a triangle by placing vectors tip‑to‑tail; the side that closes the triangle is the resultant. The component method breaks each vector into orthogonal components (usually along x and y axes) and adds those components algebraically to obtain the resultant. Both methods yield the same result for any set of coplanar vectors, and both are valid for any vectors, not just forces. Hence options A, B, and D contain inaccuracies.

mcqs.question: Two vectors \(\vec P\) and \(\vec Q\) have magnitudes 5 N and 12 N respectively and the angle between them is 60°. Using the parallelogram law, what is the magnitude of the resultant vector?
mcqs.explanation: The parallelogram law gives \(R = \sqrt{P^{2}+Q^{2}+2PQ\cos\theta}\). Substituting the values: \(R = \sqrt{5^{2}+12^{2}+2\times5\times12\times\cos60^{\circ}} = \sqrt{25+144+60} = \sqrt{229} \approx 15.13\) N, which rounds to 15.1 N. Options A, B, and D are obtained by incorrect arithmetic or by neglecting the cosine term.
